name: Kernobee
summary: In Gnomeregan, Kernobee lies trapped among the ruins. The goblin engineer found Dark Iron dwarves working on the great super rig, then was captured, beaten unconscious, and left among the troggs in the dormitory quarters.

sections.title: A Deadly Discovery
sections.body: While doing business or scavenging in Gnomeregan, Kernobee learned that Dark Iron dwarves had helped build and operate the great super rig burrowing beneath the city. He knew the danger of that discovery and tried to flee to Ratchet. There he meant to warn his associate, Tinkerwiz. The Dark Irons caught him before he could escape.

sections.title: Left for the Troggs
sections.body: Kernobee's captors beat him unconscious and left him alive. They threw him into a small room along the dormitory corridor, opposite the Clean Zone. Feral troggs and radiation surround him. He needs help to wake, reach safety, and escape the ruins.

faq.answer: Kernobee is a goblin operative found unconscious in Gnomeregan's dormitory sector. He works closely with Tinkerwiz in Ratchet and entered the ruins before his attackers caught him.

faq.q: Why was Kernobee imprisoned in Gnomeregan?
aliases: why did dark irons capture him
faq.answer: Kernobee discovered that the Dark Iron clan was helping build subterranean super rig machines inside Gnomeregan. The Dark Irons knocked him unconscious and threw him into the dormitory to die, keeping their presence and sabotage quiet.
Kernobee reports to Tinkerwiz, a goblin engineer in Ratchet, the neutral port town across the sea in the Barrens.

faq.q: Where in Gnomeregan is Kernobee located?
faq.answer: Kernobee lies unconscious in a small side room on the Dormitory's lower level, on its western side directly across from the Clean Zone.

angles.text: For gnomes fighting to reclaim their homeland, Kernobee's discovery shows that Dark Iron dwarves aided their catastrophe from the shadows.
As an engineer, you know the danger of exploring experimental subterranean machinery like the Dark Iron rigs while rival schematics are at stake.
